pr_body:
## Description
Added enableRangeProcessing parameter to TypedResult.Stream(...)

Fixes #47557
pr_comments: Thanks for your PR, @DanielBryars. Someone from the team will get assigned to your PR shortly and we'll get it reviewed.
The API needs to be approved before this PR moves forward. Also this looks like a breaking change?

Looks like this PR hasn't been active for some time and the codebase could have been changed in the meantime.
To make sure no breaking changes are introduced, please leave an `/azp run` comment here to rerun the CI pipeline and confirm success before merging the change.

This PR is incomplete, it doesn't actually process ranges on the given stream. Doing such processing would require adding a wrapper around the stream passed to the callback that discarded data written to it that was outside of the range. This would not be a good way of serving responses, there's no way to efficiently seek through the data or stop once the range has been fulfilled. You're better off writing directly to the response body in your endpoint. In doing so, you have an opportunity to limit how much data you produce based on the range requested.

issue_context.title: Update TypedResults.Stream to include optional enableRangeProcessing parameter, or change documentation.
comments:
Fixing this would be awkward, the callback is doing the writing directly to the server, but the callback doesn't have the range parameters.
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/419065590260e6597a994007512d03736e744da1/src/Http/Http.Results/src/PushStreamHttpResult.cs#L109-L121

If ranges were enabled, the stream passed to the callback would have to be a wrapper that dropped all content written to the stream except for the expected range. That's pretty in-efficient. I think we're better off not supporting this and updating the docs.

Thank you for submitting this for API review. This will be reviewed by @dotnet/aspnet-api-review at the next meeting of the ASP.NET Core API Review group. Please ensure you take a look at [the API review process documentation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/docs/APIReviewProcess.md) and ensure that:

* The PR contains changes to the reference-assembly that describe the API change. **Or**, you have included a snippet of reference-assembly-style code that illustrates the API change.
* The PR describes the impact to users, both positive (useful new APIs) and negative (breaking changes).
* Someone is assigned to "champion" this change in the meeting, and they understand the impact and design of the change.

API Review Notes:

- Unlike the existing `enableRangeProcessing` overloads that takes a file name, the stream parameter to the func will always have to waste resource draining data ahead of and after the requested range. This seems as bad or worse than the `PipeReader` overload in that respect though.

We don't think this is high value. It could lead to poor performance, and the implementation would be complicated. API rejected.

review_comments:
This will cause ranges to be calculated and headers set, but it doesn't actually serve the correct content. The callback doesn't know which range to server.
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/419065590260e6597a994007512d03736e744da1/src/Http/Http.Results/src/PushStreamHttpResult.cs#L109-L121
FYI we avoid binary breaking changes like this, existing APIs cannot be modified, even if it's source compatible, this would have to be a whole new method.
